hypotheses: For a new preregistered study of nonoverlapping prospective 168h episodes, no-typed-warning ETH states have a more negative median subsequent maximum adverse excursion, in percent, than comparable typed-warning ETH states. Falsified if their episode-level median is no more negative. This tests whether the descriptive no-warning pattern survives removal of overlapping freezes; it does not define an action rule.

For newly preregistered forecast tests with target units and scientific-admission requirements fixed before outcomes, at least one matured outcome will be scientifically score-eligible. Falsified if none is eligible after those new tests mature. Existing tests and their definitions remain unchanged.
summary: The milestone adds matured evidence, but no forecast-skill learning claim is supported: every listed matured experiment candidate remains inconclusive with zero scientific-score-eligible outcomes. The highest-information bounded question is whether adverse excursions observed without typed warnings persist at the level of independent prospective episodes. Descriptive protection results challenge any assumption that a missing warning means little subsequent downside, but neither a missed-warning rate nor a market rule has been established. This is an evidence-milestone review, not a completed November monthly review.
uncertainties: Independent adverse-event counts and the effect of overlapping freezes on protection-calibration medians are unknown.
Scientific-admission status is null for the listed matured candidates; the supplied evidence does not explain their zero eligible-outcome counts.
